A dispatch the program itself does not pin down (TestUnresolvedDispatchIsReported).
NewRunner has no body — nothing in the program says which Runner it returns — so
the call graph resolves r.Go() to no callee, while a CHA candidate (Loud.Go)
spawns. The audit must REPORT that dispatch, naming the method and its call
site, rather than union the candidates or wave it through.

-- cmd.go --
package unresolvedcmd

import (
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"

	"example.com/fixture/unresolvedlib"
)

// Blind dispatches on a Runner it cannot see into.
func Blind() *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use: "blind",
		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
			r := unresolvedlib.NewRunner()
			return r.Go()
		},
	}
}

-- lib.go --
package unresolvedlib

import "os/exec"

type Runner interface{ Go() error }

// NewRunner is declared without a body: its result is opaque to the program.
func NewRunner() Runner

type Loud struct{}

func (Loud) Go() error { return exec.Command("git", "gc").Run() }

type Quiet struct{}

func (Quiet) Go() error { return nil }
